title: SpaceX Exposure Verification Desk for Advisors
one_liner: A due-diligence service that tells advisors and retail investors whether a 'SpaceX exposure' SPV actually holds anything, and flags impersonation and deepfake endorsements timed to launch and IPO news.
customer: Registered investment advisers, family offices, broker-dealer compliance teams and private-bank due-diligence desks being pitched SPVs and notes marketed as SpaceX or Starlink exposure. Secondary: sophisticated retail via a subscription.
problem: Demand for SpaceX exposure is intense (Starlink about 12M subscribers, $11.4B 2025 revenue, Starship reached orbit on 28 Sept 2026), but shares are transfer-restricted, so anything offered is indirect: SPVs of SPVs with stacked fees, sold over LinkedIn, WhatsApp and Telegram, some holding nothing. Deepfake Musk endorsements and fake launch livestreams add a scam layer. Lumpy events such as the 16 Sept 2026 Valor distribution add confusion about what is real.
solution: (1) Map every SPV using SpaceX or Starlink naming from SEC Form D and adviser filings, with sponsor history, fee stacks and upstream fund lineage. (2) Holdings attestation by obtaining custodian, transfer agent or upstream-fund confirmation. (3) Compare marketing claims against issuer transfer restrictions and last known tender pricing. (4) A red-flag score (offshore layers, unlicensed sellers, cloned domains) and an alert feed on new offerings and impersonation around launch days and any listing.
why_now: IPO speculation, the Valor stock distribution on 16 Sept 2026, Starship's orbital flight and a record Golden Dome and launch boom are all feeding retail FOMO. Scam economics are inverting (tools cost about $50 while average payments rose 253%) and AI deepfakes are cheap. If a listing happens, the desk pivots to lock-up and SPV-unwind verification, so it does not depend on one date.
revenue_model: $750-2,500 per SPV verification report, $499 per month for adviser subscriptions with alerts, and enterprise seats for compliance teams. Later expansion to other hot pre-IPO space names.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not access to SpaceX but the truth about what an SPV holds. The key facts (Form D filings, fee layers, issuer restrictions) are public and cheap to analyze, yet every hype cycle mints exposure products faster than compliance staff can diligence. Buyers pay for a signed opinion that gives them cover to say no.
first_30_days: Scrape EDGAR for SpaceX and Starlink SPV names and publish an 'SPV Layer Map' with fee stacks. Send it to 200 RIAs and compliance officers. Offer 3 free verifications, then sell the next ones at $1,500. Set up domain-impersonation monitoring keyed to launch dates. Position as research and diligence, not investment advice.

title: Funding Waterfall at the Vet Estimate
one_liner: Front-desk software that routes each vet estimate to the cheapest available funding: insurance advance, charity grant, clinic plan, or credit.
customer: Independent and affordable-care vet clinics as the subscriber. Charitable funds and lenders are paying counterparties.
problem: 85% of vet professionals say clients decline care at estimates of $1,000 or less, and 13% of euthanasias are attributed to inability to pay. Funding sources exist but are fragmented: reimbursement-model insurers pay weeks later, dozens of small charity funds are unknown at the front desk, and mainstream medical credit charges clinics steep fees. New philanthropy has no distribution pipe, so grants like Duffield's are hard to place and audit.
solution: An 'estimate inbox' where the front desk emails or prints the estimate, with no PIMS integration. Within minutes it returns a ranked stack: (1) a 0% claim advance for insured pets secured by the expected reimbursement; (2) pre-screened charity or grant matches; (3) a clinic-carried 0% plan backed by a shared default-guarantee pool; (4) conventional credit. One application, one payout to the clinic in 24-48 hours, with compliance reporting for funders.
why_now: The Duffield Foundation committed $250M over 5 years on Sept 17, 2026 (first grants: 250 x $10K plus $10M multi-year), building on PetSmart Charities' $100M pledge. Neither has pipes for high-volume, low-friction placement. Insurance premiums are up 19.7% against animals up 9%, and clinics are being coached on money conversations. Instant payment rails let clinics be paid the same day.
revenue_model: Clinics pay 1-2% of routed funding or $199 a month. Funders pay about 5% of grant flow as an admin fee, which is cheaper than their own staff. Lenders pay origination fees.
non_obvious_insight: The decline decision is made in a 90-second front-desk moment, and every funding source is built for a different moment. Whoever owns the estimate document owns the routing, and philanthropic money is desperate for a distribution pipe with audit trails.
first_30_days: Sign 15 independent clinics in one metro and run the waterfall as a concierge service with spreadsheets and email. Approach one small pet charity and apply as an infrastructure partner to the Duffield programme. Find one claim-advance lender willing to take insurer-receivable risk on a pilot basis.

title: Book the Unbookable: Agents for Offline Suppliers
one_liner: A voice-and-WhatsApp agent phones, negotiates and confirms bookings with small inns, guides and boat operators that have no API, then turns each one into bookable inventory.
customer: Independent travel advisors and small DMCs first, later AI trip-planning apps and OTAs seeking long-tail inventory.
problem: The best small inns, agriturismi, ryokan, guides and boat operators take bookings by phone, WhatsApp or email in local languages, with deposits by bank transfer. Advisors spend hours per booking, AI agents cannot book them and OTAs do not list them. Hotel-side voice AI is crowded (for example Dextr AI's seed), but buyer-side is empty.
solution: A real-time multilingual voice and text agent calls or messages the supplier, checks availability, negotiates a net rate within the advisor's limits and sends the deposit. A human verifies the money step. Every completed booking builds a structured supplier profile (hours, languages, deposit rules) that becomes API-bookable next time.
why_now: Real-time voice models now handle 30+ languages, WhatsApp Business is universal, and agentic payment tooling exists. Shrinking booking lead times and rerouted travel create demand for fast alternatives beyond OTA inventory.
revenue_model: USD 20-60 or 3-5% of booking value per booking from advisors, SaaS for DMCs, and later a take rate from suppliers and inventory data licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Long-tail supply is invisible to agents because it lacks an API, not because it lacks quality. The cheapest API is a phone call made by a machine with a human closing the money step, and each call builds an inventory graph nobody owns.
first_30_days: Pick Japan, Italy and Greece. Recruit 15 independent travel advisors and process 100 bookings semi-manually with human voice operators shadowing the agent at USD 30 per booking. Measure time saved and conversion.

title: Search-Fund Accelerator for Buying Scrap Yards
one_liner: A cohort program that turns laid-off mid-career managers into owner-operators of small scrap yards, e-scrap shops and transfer stations. It brings deal sourcing, environmental diligence and SBA-lender access.
customer: Laid-off ops, finance and product managers with severance or savings of about $100-300K, who pay cohort tuition and a success fee. Second customer: retiring owners of scrap and recycling businesses who want a successor buyer. SBA lenders are a channel.
problem: Mid-career job searches now run 7-13 months with near-zero interview rates (HN threads), and the hiring freeze is hitting degree-holders. Meanwhile thousands of owner-run recycling businesses have no successor. Their storage and processing permits take years to obtain, and domestic scrap has just become strategic: the Aug 27, 2026 BIS rule forces black mass and tungsten scrap sellers to allocate 100% of sales to US buyers. Nobody packages this asset class for a first-time buyer.
solution: Build a target database from state solid-waste and hazardous-waste permit records, scrap-dealer licenses and owner age. Provide a standard diligence pack covering environmental liabilities and Phase I/II, fire history and insurance, permit transferability, commodity exposure and offtake contracts. Add a 90-day operator bootcamp with a mentor operator and introductions to SBA lenders. Take a fixed fee at close plus a small advisory equity stake.
why_now: AI-driven hiring freezes are producing a large pool of capable managers with cash and time. Greenfield battery and plastics recycling is capital-destroying (Ascend Elements and Li-Cycle bankruptcies, 7 of about 30 US PET reclaimers closed), while boring, permitted, cash-flowing yards look safer. DoD and DOE equity stakes and the BIS allocation rule are re-rating domestic scrap.
revenue_model: Cohort tuition (about $4-6K per seat). Buy-side success fee ($25-50K or 1.5-2% at close). 2-5% advisory equity in each acquisition. Sell-side listing fees from retiring owners. Diligence-pack licensing to lenders.
non_obvious_insight: In recycling the scarce input is not technology or capital but a competent successor operator, and the labor market is now manufacturing them. Permits are the moat, so the right move is to buy permitted cash flow instead of financing new plants.
first_30_days: Pull permit and owner-age lists for two states. Run a free webinar for laid-off managers through layoff-tracker and career communities and enroll a first cohort of about 10. Get two retiring owners to sign exclusive sell-side LOIs. Sign an environmental-consulting partner for a flat-fee diligence pack, and one SBA lender as the financing partner.

title: Valet Keys for Delegated Browser Sessions
one_liner: An enforcement layer that lets an agent act inside your logged-in bank, airline or supplier portal, but only within per-site limits such as read-only here and a spend cap there.
customer: Enterprise finance-ops, revenue-cycle and logistics teams running browser agents on portals with no API (20-500 seats), followed by builders of prosumer browser agents who need a safety story.
problem: Insiders are building agent identity (OAuth for agents), but most delegated work rides on cookies in sites with no API. The agent inherits the user's full session. Browsers offer no primitive for a user to see, scope or withdraw an agent's access. If the user is legally the one who accessed the site, as the Ninth Circuit reasoned, the user owns everything the agent does with that session.
solution: A browser extension plus enforcement proxy with per-site policy packs that classify actions (view, draft, submit, pay, change credentials) using URL, DOM and network patterns. Irreversible actions are denied by default, with spend and count caps, step-up approval and signed action receipts. Ship maintained packs for the top 200 enterprise portals (payer, carrier, marketplace seller-center and bank portals) and update them as sites change.
why_now: Browser agents went mainstream in 2026, and about 21,600 OpenClaw instances were found exposed. Machine identities outnumber humans roughly 109 to 1, and the agent-equals-user doctrine puts liability on the delegating user.
revenue_model: $15-40 per seat per month for enterprises, policy-pack subscriptions, and a per-session API price for agent vendors.
non_obvious_insight: The missing primitive is a valet key (parks the car, cannot open the trunk) for sessions. The moat is the maintained per-site action taxonomy, which is tedious, unglamorous and hard to copy.
first_30_days: Find one revenue-cycle or logistics ops team already using browser agents and build read-only plus draft-only policy packs for the 5 portals they use. Run a $2k/month pilot and log blocked actions as proof of value.

title: GST Credit Recovery on UPI Fees
one_liner: Recover the 18% GST on new UPI MDR fees as input credit for retailers and distributors that will otherwise never claim it.
customer: GST-registered mobile, FMCG and pharma retailers and distributors in India, and their chartered accountants.
problem: From Oct 15 the 0.4% MDR carries 18% GST, and AICPDF estimates a Rs 7,000-9,000 Cr burden on distributors. Small businesses will not reconcile bulk PSP fee invoices to GSTR-2B, so credit is left unclaimed.
solution: Ingest PSP settlement reports, match fee invoices to GSTR-2B, flag missing credits and produce claim workpapers for CAs. Composition-scheme dealers are ineligible and must be screened out. The wedge is retailer associations already mobilising over the fee.
why_now: MDR starts Oct 15 and retailer bodies are organised around a 'No UPI Day' on Oct 2.
revenue_model: 10-15% of recovered credit, or Rs 499-1,999 per month per business.
non_obvious_insight: The protest is about the 0.4%. The GST layer is partly recoverable money nobody is discussing, and associations will trade it for a visible win for members.
first_30_days: Build reconciliation for PhonePe and Paytm settlement file formats and sign two retailer associations.

title: Verifier-Ready Emissions Data Rooms for CBAM Exporters
one_liner: A metering-to-evidence pipeline that gives small non-EU steel, aluminum and fertilizer producers a clean, pre-audited data room for accredited verifiers, so their EU and UK buyers stop defaulting to punitive default values.
customer: Producers and processors with 50-500 employees in Turkey, India, Egypt, Vietnam, Ukraine and South Africa (steel re-rollers, extruders, wire and fastener makers, fertilizer blenders). Paid by the producer or subsidized by the EU/UK importer buying from them.
problem: CBAM entered its definitive phase in 2026 and UK CBAM starts 1 Jan 2027 across 8 sectors. Importers lacking actual emissions data fall back on default values, which carry a mark-up (background, verify). Accredited verifiers are scarce, and small producers keep energy invoices in spreadsheets with no monitoring plan, so verification is slow and expensive and importers cannot get usable data.
solution: A two-week onboarding: connect electricity and gas meters or invoices, production logs and precursor traceability, then generate the monitoring methodology plan, the emissions report in CBAM format and an evidence index. Internal pre-verification, hand-off to partner verifiers, quarterly refresh, and sharing of the verified data with each importer through an API.
why_now: The definitive period began in 2026, verification of 2026 imports lands in 2027, and UK CBAM begins in three months. Default-value cost pressure now exceeds the price of proper data collection.
revenue_model: EUR 6-25k/year per plant (producer-paid or importer-sponsored supplier program) plus a coordination fee per verification.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone sells CBAM to the EU importer's finance team. The bottleneck is evidence-poor factories and verifier capacity upstream. Importers will fund supplier readiness because default values cost more than the tool, and verified plant data is reusable across every EU and UK customer of that plant.
first_30_days: Find three EU or UK importers of steel wire or fasteners with Turkish or Indian suppliers (trade fairs, LinkedIn) and offer a supplier-readiness pilot for five plants at EUR 3k each. Deliver with templates and spreadsheets and partner with one or two verifiers.

title: Closure-as-a-Service for Colleges and Grad Programs
one_liner: Orchestrating orderly teach-outs, transcript custody and student transfers for shutting colleges and graduate programs that the new loan caps and demographics are about to gut.
customer: Small private colleges and graduate programs facing closure or merger, state higher-ed regulators, accreditors, and university systems absorbing programs.
problem: The enrollment cliff plus the end of Grad PLUS and the new caps push small colleges and grad programs (nursing, counseling and others) below viability. Closures are chaotic: teach-out agreements, records custody, transfer-credit mapping, refunds and student communications are improvised, and regulators and accreditors demand teach-out plans.
solution: A standing playbook, software and partner network: pre-negotiated teach-out partners, an AI-assisted transfer-credit mapper across receiving schools, secure transcript and records custody, student communications, and tracking of closure obligations. Sell a 'teach-out readiness audit' and retainer to at-risk institutions before they need it.
why_now: The July 2026 aid reset, K-12 and college demographic cliffs and rising closures make this a recurring workload. State regulators are searching for standard processes.
revenue_model: $20-50k annual readiness retainers, $100-400k per closure project, $5-15 per student per year records custody, and referral fees from receiving institutions.
non_obvious_insight: Institutions treat closure as a one-time catastrophe, but with hundreds at risk it is a recurring, standardizable service, like a bankruptcy trustee, where fees come from the estate and reputation for orderly process determines who gets hired.
first_30_days: Publish a teach-out readiness checklist. Offer a $7.5k readiness audit to 10 small colleges and 2 state regulators. Recruit an ex-registrar and an ex-accreditation consultant as delivery leads.

title: Forever Guardian: Lifetime Care After Parents Are Gone
one_liner: A prepaid, life-insurance-funded successor-care plan in which a named team becomes the lifelong advocate, money manager and care coordinator for an adult with a disability after the parents are gone.
customer: Parents in their 60s-80s of adult children with intellectual or developmental disabilities (nearly one million US households have adults with I/DD living with an aging caregiver). Referred by special-needs planning attorneys and financial planners.
problem: Parents dread 'who will look after them when we're gone.' Siblings are often unavailable, state Medicaid waiver waitlists are long, pooled special-needs trusts manage money but rarely relationships, and no single accountable person exists for decades. The current autism generation is about to become adults, and the adult cohort will surge.
solution: A tiered plan. (1) While parents are alive: a named care manager, annual home visit, a living 'letter of intent' binder (routines, medications, preferences), and monthly check-in calls, so the person already knows the successor. (2) At transition: the team acts as advocate or guardian-of-record where allowed, coordinates services, audits group-home quality, and works with a partner trust company holding a pooled special-needs trust. (3) Funded by a paid-up second-to-die life policy or an upfront fee plus a monthly retainer.
why_now: Peak-65 parents are hitting the age where the successor question is urgent, Medicaid home- and community-based services are under financial pressure, and adults with I/DD are living longer than any prior generation. It is a large, emotionally urgent market with no scaled, for-profit successor-care provider.
revenue_model: Upfront enrollment ($5-15k or insurance-funded), a monthly care-management retainer ($100-200), trust administration fees through the partner, and insurance commissions.
non_obvious_insight: The real product is a relationship that starts before the parents die. The annual home visit is both the moat and the sales funnel: by the time a parent passes, the guardian is already someone the adult knows and trusts. It converts a frightening legal product into a service with visible value every month while the parents are still alive to judge it.
first_30_days: Partner with three special-needs planning attorneys and one trust company. Sign 15 families to a $1,500 'Shadow Year' (assessment, letter-of-intent binder, quarterly visits, monthly calls). Hire one care manager and validate the guardianship, trust and licensing requirements for a single state before promising the full lifetime plan.

title: Payroll-Deducted Paylater Refinance for Factory Workers
one_liner: Consolidate minimum-wage workers' paylater and online loans into one payroll-deducted instalment, sold to the employer as retention.
customer: Indonesian manufacturers and retailers with 1,000+ minimum-wage staff, especially in Java's industrial belts; employers pay a fee and a partner lender funds.
problem: Paylater financing reached Rp43.28T in May and online lending Rp100.69T, and defaults are rising among minimum-wage workers. Collection harassment causes absenteeism and turnover.
solution: Consolidate a worker's paylater and pinjol debts into one lower-rate loan repaid via payroll, funded by a licensed multifinance or bank partner. The wedge is three factories in Bekasi and Karawang.
why_now: OJK scrutiny is rising and the 2026 macro squeeze is pushing defaults up.
revenue_model: 1-2% origination plus lender spread share, and an employer fee of Rp10-15k per worker per month.
non_obvious_insight: The paylater trap is an HR problem before it is a credit problem, and the employer is the only party with payroll access and a reason to care.
first_30_days: Interview HR heads at three factories and pilot with 200 workers using a partner lender.

title: H-2A Housing-as-a-Service for Growers
one_liner: Lease pre-certified modular seasonal housing by the bed so growers can actually use H-2A visas.
customer: Specialty-crop growers and farm labor contractors in CA, WA, GA and the Southeast.
problem: Immigration enforcement removed at least 155,000 farm workers and H-2A is projected to grow toward 500k jobs, but employers must supply inspected housing, which is scarce and slow to build.
solution: A fleet of modular bunk units that pass DOL and OSHA housing inspection, delivered to farms or leased sites for the season, with paperwork and maintenance handled.
why_now: The October 2025 wage-rule change and enforcement-driven crew losses push growers to H-2A at scale, making beds the binding constraint.
revenue_model: Per-bed-month lease of roughly $X seasonal contracts with multi-year renewals.
non_obvious_insight: Visa wages get the headlines, but whoever owns compliant beds owns the labor channel. Housing is asset-backed, financeable and repeats every season.
first_30_days: Pre-sell 100 beds for the 2027 season to five growers with deposits, source used modular units, and get one prototype unit through a state housing inspection.

title: Medicaid Look-Back Packet Builder
one_liner: Turn 60 months of messy bank statements into a caseworker-ready Medicaid application packet with explanations, so families avoid 'failure to provide verification' denials.
customer: Adult children and POA agents applying for nursing-home Medicaid for a parent ($299-$499 per case), plus elder-law and Medicaid-planning firms and senior placement advisors ($500-$1,500/month seats or per-case fees).
problem: Long-term-care Medicaid reviews up to 60 months of statements for every open account and every account closed within the window. Caseworkers typically demand written explanations for each expenditure over about $500. If records are missing the application is likely denied for 'failure to provide verification'. POA agents often lack online access to old or closed accounts, and banks can charge research fees for paper copies. Meanwhile the parent's care bills accumulate and elder-law attorneys charge thousands.
solution: Upload statements (PDF, CSV or bank link) and use OCR and an LLM to build the ledger. Detect large transfers, gifts, transfers to relatives and round-number withdrawals. Show likely penalty-period exposure. Draft the explanation letters and a caseworker index with state-specific checklists. Auto-generate missing-statement request letters to banks with a POA cover page, track which accounts are still missing, and hand the attorney a clean exception report. A separate 'consolidate and simplify before you need Medicaid' mode targets families planning ahead.
why_now: Document extraction and bank-data aggregation now make a 60-month review a minutes-long task rather than paralegal hours. Federal law (H.R. 1) sets a $1M Medicaid home-equity cap from Jan 1, 2028, and the 2026 baseline is $752,000 in most states, so more middle-class families in expensive housing markets will need spend-down or planning. State caseworkers will also be stretched by the 2027 work-requirement rollout, making complete first-time packets more valuable.
revenue_model: $299-$499 per family packet, $99 'look-back risk scan' as a lead magnet, and $500-$1,500/month firm seats or $75-$150 per case for elder-law offices, with placement-advisor referral fees as a secondary channel.
non_obvious_insight: The denial reason is paperwork, not eligibility: the requirement to explain each $500+ transaction and produce statements for closed accounts is a software-shaped burden that elder-law attorneys currently bill by the hour. See the documentation rules and 'likely deny for failure to provide verification' language at https://www.paelderlaw.net/medicaid-application-process-5-year-look-back-5-years-of-records-for-small-and-inactive-accounts/. The home-equity change is at https://justiceinaging.org/hr1-imposes-new-limit-on-home-equity-for-medicaid-ltss-effective-2028/. Bank refusal to deal with POA agents compounds it (https://www.aarp.org/caregiving/financial-legal/power-of-attorney-bank-approval/). Reddit was unreachable, so this rests on legal-practice and AARP sources describing the recurring r/AgingParents 'Mom needs Medicaid, what do they want?' situation.
first_30_days: Start with one state with clear caseworker checklists (Pennsylvania or New York). Hand-build 5 packets for free for local elder-law paralegals to validate the exception logic, then productize statement parsing and letter generation. Sell a $99 risk scan and a $349 packet through caregiver Facebook groups and 3-5 elder-law and placement-advisor partners, aiming for 10 paid packets and one firm pilot.

title: Referee Pathway: Officiating as a School Credential
one_liner: A semester-long, credit-bearing officiating course that puts teens in mentored cohorts on paid youth games, fixing the referee shortage by fixing retention.
customer: District CTE directors and state high-school athletic associations are the buyers. Youth leagues and game assignors are paying placement partners. Students (14+ where state rules allow) are the beneficiaries.
problem: Youth and high-school games are shortened or cancelled for lack of officials. Widely cited surveys say most new officials quit within two years, largely because of abuse from parents and fans. Meanwhile teens lack decent first jobs, entry-level white-collar hiring has cracked, and districts are chasing CTE pathways that lead to real work.
solution: A CTE elective, 'Officiating and Conflict Management'. Students learn rules, mechanics, film review and de-escalation role-play. They then work mentored, paid assignments as a cohort (never alone) at rec-league games, with body-worn cameras or comms for protection. The output is a portable 'Registered Official' credential aligned with the state association's licensing. We sell curriculum, assignment scheduling and an insurance wrapper.
why_now: The officials shortage has persisted since COVID and many states have passed laws penalizing assault on officials. CTE enrollment is rising (vocational-heavy public two-years grew 11.7% in Spring 2025). After the entry-level AI job shock, schools and parents want credentials tied to human judgment. Sports is one of the few settings where judgment under pressure is the actual job.
revenue_model: $150-300 per student license paid by districts from CTE budgets. An 8-10% platform fee on paid assignments (typically $40-80 per game). State-association sponsorships and body-cam/insurance partner rebates. A 40-student district cohort is roughly $8-12k plus assignment fees.
non_obvious_insight: The shortage is a retention problem caused by isolation and abuse in an official's first 20 games, not a recruiting problem. A school cohort is the only structure that gives new officials a team, a mentor and institutional backing. De-escalating under hostile scrutiny is also a transferable credential for security, hospitality, HR and healthcare jobs.
first_30_days: Pitch 2-3 CTE directors and the local officials' association. Run a 10-12 week after-school pilot for 30 students, funded by a rec league or booster at about $99 per student. Track how many are still officiating a season later against the roughly 20% baseline. Use the retention data and a league letter of support to pitch the state association.

title: Parametric Recovery Cover for Tourism Towns
one_liner: Annual parametric policies bought by destination tourism boards that pay out within days when fire, smoke, flood or road closures crater visitor demand, even with no physical damage.
customer: Destination marketing organizations and county or city tourism authorities in single-access, hazard-exposed resort towns (Estes Park, Truckee/Tahoe, Big Bear, Gatlinburg, Outer Banks, Asheville, Maui), funded by lodging taxes (transient occupancy tax, TOT) with $50-500K premium budgets.
problem: Business-interruption cover requires physical damage, and civil-authority riders are short. After Lahaina, Asheville and Caldor, the losses came from closed roads, smoke and perception, not damaged hotels. TOT revenue funds recovery marketing and services, and it collapses exactly when the town most needs to advertise. Retail insurers are retreating from these towns and small lodging and restaurants cannot buy adequate cover.
solution: We design tourism-specific indices and place the cover. Triggers use hazard evidence (evacuation orders, AQI days over threshold, DOT road-closure days) confirmed by an occupancy drop versus baseline (STR/hotel data such as AirDNA). Payout scales are calibrated to historical TOT dips. The policyholder is the DMO, which re-grants through its existing marketing and small-business grant programs. Capacity comes from a fronting carrier or parametric MGA plus reinsurers and ILS. We deliver index design, backtests, placement and the claims data oracle.
why_now: Reinsurance is softening fast: Howden reports property-cat risk-adjusted rates down up to 25% at 1 June 2026 after -16% and -14.7% earlier, with record capital (about $790B, secondary source). Niche capacity is now cheap while retail carriers still retreat. Cat bond issuance hit records in H1 2026 (about $18B). Travel booking windows are about 33 days, so a fast cash-funded comeback campaign can restore bookings quickly.
revenue_model: Broker/MGA-style commission of 12-18% of premium, plus index licensing and annual re-modeling fees. Ten towns at about $150K average premium and 15% commission is roughly $225K in year one, scaling through state travel associations.
non_obvious_insight: Tourism loss after disasters is mostly access and perception, not damage. A public tourism board is the rare buyer that can purchase parametric cover and redistribute it to small businesses that could never qualify individually. The lodging-tax series is a clean, public, monthly loss history no adjuster touched. Public-entity buyers also sidestep the homeowner rate-filing regime that strangles retail products.
first_30_days: Backtest four past events (East Troublesome/Estes Park 2020, Caldor/Tahoe 2021, Lahaina 2023, Helene/Asheville 2024) using public TOT reports, AQI and road-closure logs. Produce 'what you would have received' one-pagers. Pitch 10 DMO executive directors and 3 state travel associations. Get a parametric MGA or fronting partner to quote. Target the first bound policy in the spring 2027 budget and fire-season renewal window.

title: Independent Lab Certifying AI Detectors and Watermarks
one_liner: An AV-TEST-style lab that red-teams detectors and watermarks every month and sells certification seals and buyer reports.
customer: Detection and watermark vendors (seals and re-tests), and enterprise buyers such as platform trust-and-safety teams, publishers, insurers and law firms that need to know which tool to trust.
problem: Detection is crowded and cheap (Pangram $9M raise at $20/month, GPTZero $10M, GetReal $18M, Reality Defender $15M, Deezer licensing its detector) and buyers cannot verify accuracy claims. Pangram claims about 1 in 10,000 false positives, yet a reviewer still saw human sentences flagged. Watermark removers appeared within a week of Sora. Public 'human vs AI' scores now shape reputations, but no one audits them.
solution: A monthly adversarial benchmark across text, audio, image and video. It uses stratified known-human gold sets (for example non-native English writers and niche music genres), fresh output from current models, adaptive attacks (paraphrasers, re-encoding, watermark removers) and fixed false-positive operating points. Publish a leaderboard, and issue 'certified at or below X% false-positive rate on domain Y' seals and watermark robustness ratings.
why_now: Detectors are being embedded in reader-facing features (Substack, LinkedIn, Deezer licensing), EU Art. 50 pushes marking and detection into procurement checklists, and reputational stakes for false positives are visible.
revenue_model: $15-60k/year per vendor for testing and seals, $5-25k/year buyer subscriptions for detailed results, and $10-40k custom bake-offs.
non_obvious_insight: When the buyer cannot verify a product's core claim, the independent tester captures value, which is why UL, AV-TEST and NSS Labs exist. The scarce asset is a fresh, curated, known-human gold set plus an adversarial toolkit.
first_30_days: Publish a free benchmark v0 of six text detectors and three audio detectors in three weeks, using 2,000 volunteer-written human documents and fresh AI outputs. DM vendors and trust-and-safety leads with a paid 'verified retest' offer. First payers will be challengers who want a credible badge.

title: Time-to-First-Part: Install Readiness for Machine Dealers
one_liner: A pre-delivery site-scan and commissioning package that gets backlogged machines cutting parts weeks sooner.
customer: Machine-tool, laser and robot dealers and OEM sales teams, plus 20-200 employee manufacturers buying their first big machine.
problem: Unfilled capital-goods orders sit at $953B after a record $85.9B in July orders. Much of it lands in old buildings with no as-built drawings. Machines arrive to floors, doors, crane paths and utility drops that cannot take them, so crated $500k machines sit idle. Dealers often get paid only at acceptance.
solution: A 20-minute phone or LiDAR walkthrough becomes an as-built model. Software checks the machine footprint, door and aisle clearance and rigging path, flags slab and vibration issues (with a ground-penetrating-radar partner), lists air, coolant and chip-handling needs, and produces a rigging plan and punch list. It can also dispatch vetted riggers and millwrights.
why_now: Reshoring is happening inside existing walls, the equipment backlog is at a record, and riggers and millwrights are scarce. Phone-based 3D capture (LiDAR, Gaussian splats) has matured.
revenue_model: $1.2-3k per site package, paid by the dealer or bundled into the machine price. 10-15% referral on rigging. Dealer team subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Dealers get paid at acceptance, so time-to-first-part is their cash-flow metric and they will pay to shorten it. The unfilled-order backlog hides a second backlog of installed-but-not-producing machines.
first_30_days: Sign three regional dealers (CNC, laser or robot) for a pilot. Do 10 scans with iPhones. Produce a sample report. Measure install days saved against comparable installs.

title: Advance Hotels Their Stuck OTA Payouts
one_liner: A neutral lender advances 90-95% of completed-stay OTA payouts on checkout day for a flat 1.5-2% fee, so independent hotels stop financing the OTAs.
customer: Independent hotels and small groups of 20-150 rooms in Europe with 60-80% of bookings through Booking.com, Expedia or Agoda.
problem: Insiders treat OTA payment collection as a convenience. In practice about 70% of Booking Holdings' 2025 bookings used its payment service, and hotels are paid after checkout. That is weeks of float while they pay staff, energy and suppliers at costs that have repriced sharply since the Hormuz shock. Banks cannot see these receivables, so nobody underwrites them.
solution: Read reservation and payout schedules from the hotel's channel manager or extranet export. Underwrite each receivable, which is checked out and has a scheduled payout from a top-three OTA. Advance the cash the same day, and sweep repayment when the OTA pays. Later, extend to advances on confirmed future stays for seasonal cash needs.
why_now: OTA merchant payments became the majority path in 2025. Energy and construction costs repriced after the March 2026 Hormuz closure, and capital is described as disciplined and selective. Open banking and embedded-finance rails make small-ticket receivables lending workable for a small team.
revenue_model: A 1.2-2.5% fee per advance, which is about 20-40% annualised on 2-4 week paper, funded by a credit-fund warehouse line, with a small servicing fee.
non_obvious_insight: The merchant model quietly turned hotels into unpriced lenders to OTAs. A checked-out receivable from a top-three OTA is close to risk-free collateral that has never been packaged, because lenders cannot see reservation-level data.
first_30_days: Line up EUR 300-500K from a specialty credit fund or family office. Recruit 5 independent hotels through revenue-management consultants and hotel associations. Offer to advance manually against payout statements they email, testing repayment on the next OTA payout before building any integration.

title: Contingency Recovery of Missed Rotable Repair Warranties
one_liner: A success-fee auditor that finds repaired aircraft components that failed inside the shop's warranty window, and turns them into filed claims and cash.
customer: Small and mid-size operators with their own stores and a thin materials team. That means regional airlines, Part 135 cargo feeders and air-ambulance fleets, and Part 145 shops that buy their own exchange units. They pay 20-25% of whatever cash or credit is recovered, and nothing up front.
problem: A repaired starter-generator, bleed valve, hydraulic pump or fuel control that fails 4 months after the shop visit is often covered by warranty. Almost nobody claims it. The tech pulling the unit at 3 AM is trying to make a 6 AM departure and never sees the warranty terms. The repair invoice sits in accounts payable as a PDF. The removal record sits in the maintenance system, and hours and cycles sit in a third place. One materials coordinator owns thousands of removals a year, with 30-90 day claim windows. Three other leaks go unclaimed as well: 'no fault found' evaluation fees on units that were still under warranty, unreturned exchange cores that turn into penalty charges, and repair turnaround-time guarantees that shops never credit because nobody compares PO date to receipt date.
solution: Ingest three exports: removals and installs, PO and repair invoices (PDFs read with an LLM extractor), and the negotiated warranty terms. Match by part number and serial number, including interchangeable P/Ns. Flag every in-warranty failure, late repair turn, disputable NFF fee and open core. Then draft the claim on each vendor's own template, track it to a paid credit, and re-run monthly. Add a 3 AM 'is this unit under warranty?' lookup for maintenance control, so the claim gets started at the moment of removal.
why_now: Airline cost pressure on regionals is high, and mechanic wages rose sharply in 2024-2026, so labor cost per removal is up. Materials teams are being cut while fleets stay old. LLM invoice and PDF extraction only became reliable and cheap enough in the last 18 months, and that is the missing link, because the money sits in unstructured AP documents that MRO software never reads.
revenue_model: Contingency fee of 20-25% of recovered cash and credits, with a 12-month tail on the audit. Later add a $2-5k per month SaaS tier for continuous monitoring, and sell benchmark data on shop warranty behavior to airline procurement teams.
non_obvious_insight: The leak is not in the maintenance system, it is in accounts payable. The tech who removes the part, the coordinator who could file the claim and the department that paid the invoice never share a screen. MRO software vendors will not fix it because warranty terms live in negotiated PDFs, not fields. Repair shops know most eligible claims are never filed, and they price that into their rates. A contingency auditor is the same playbook as freight-audit and telecom-audit firms, aimed at a niche nobody has covered.
first_30_days: Pitch 10 directors of maintenance and materials managers at small regionals, cargo feeders and helicopter EMS operators. Offer a free 12-month leakage audit, and ask them for the three exports. Build the matcher in Python plus an LLM invoice parser, and use a retired warranty or materials coordinator as a paid advisor for vendor quirks. Deliver a ranked claim list to the first 2-3 customers, file the claims yourself, and sign the success-fee agreement on the first credit memo. Publish the aggregate audit finding, such as the percentage of eligible failures that were never claimed, as the lead magnet.

title: DKIM for Bank Accounts: Signed Payee Records
one_liner: A free, domain-verified payment record that suppliers publish, plus an AP plug-in that blocks any bank-detail change the supplier's own domain has not signed.
customer: Bookkeeping and accounting firms, and AP teams at 20-500 person companies on QuickBooks, Xero, Bill.com or NetSuite. Suppliers publish for free.
problem: BEC cost $3.05B in 2025, about 3.4x the $893M IC3 tags as AI-related, yet the money and attention go to deepfake detection. Bank-detail change requests still arrive by email or phone and get 'verified' by calling a number supplied in the same message. Small firms have no fraud team, and 3 seconds of audio now clones the voice they trust.
solution: A supplier proves domain control (DNS TXT plus a signed JSON file: legal name, hashed account and routing numbers, valid-from and valid-to dates, rotation contacts). A browser extension and accounting-app add-on compares any vendor bank details at bill entry and payment approval against that record. It hard-warns on mismatch and routes changes through a supplier-initiated, delayed, out-of-band confirmation flow. Every check is logged as evidence for the firm's crime-insurance social-engineering endorsement.
why_now: Cloned voices and AI-written invoices have broken the callback-and-voice-check control. IC3's 2025 numbers show BEC is still the largest business loss pool. Instant rails like FedNow and RTP make wrong payments irrevocable. Accounting platforms now have open app stores that allow a third-party control at the moment of payment.
revenue_model: $5-9 per client company per month for accounting firms, or $19-29 per AP seat for in-house teams. Suppliers are free. Later, per-check API fees from payment platforms and insurer-funded discounts.
non_obvious_insight: BEC is a provenance problem for one string of digits, not a media-authenticity problem. Email fraud fell when SPF/DKIM anchored trust in domain ownership, and the same move works for payee data. Selling through accountants avoids the two-sided cold start: each supplier who publishes instantly protects every customer of theirs that uses a participating firm.
first_30_days: Publish an open spec, a Chrome extension and a read-only Xero/QuickBooks add-on. Recruit 10-15 bookkeeping firms (30-100 clients each) through ProAdvisor and bookkeeper communities. For each firm, send its 20 largest vendors a five-minute publish flow. Convert 10 firms to $99/month plans.

title: Dr. Simi USA: Pharmacy-Plus-Consult for the Uninsured
one_liner: Small-format, generic-first pharmacies with a nurse-practitioner consult room beside the counter, posted cash prices and no insurance needed, following Mexico's Farmacias Similares model and landing in US pharmacy deserts.
customer: Uninsured and underinsured adults in pharmacy deserts and immigrant neighborhoods. An estimated 4.8M Americans lost coverage after the enhanced ACA subsidies expired, and about 48M people live in pharmacy deserts. The second customer is at-risk independent pharmacists who license the clinic kit.
problem: Rite Aid is gone (all stores closed after its 2025 Chapter 11), Walgreens is shrinking, and independents are squeezed by PBM reimbursement. An uninsured person with a UTI or sinus infection faces a $150-250 urgent-care visit plus retail drug prices, so many just skip treatment.
solution: An 800-1,200 sq ft store or a 200 sq ft conversion inside an existing independent pharmacy. A flat $25-40 NP consult (loss leader), point-of-care tests (strep, flu, UTI, A1c), on-site dispensing of generics at transparent cost-plus prices, bilingual staff, and chronic-refill programs. The visit and the dispense happen in one 10-minute stop, so there is no abandoned prescription. Mexico's Farmacias Similares runs thousands of outlets with an attached doctor's office charging a few dollars.
why_now: Coverage is shrinking at the same time as pharmacy access: enhanced ACA subsidies lapsed at the end of 2025, Medicaid cuts phase in through 2026-27, and Rite Aid's liquidation left holes in low-income neighborhoods. Cost Plus Drugs has taught Americans to expect transparent generic prices, so a cash-price store is no longer strange.
revenue_model: Dispensing margin on generics, flat consult fees, point-of-care lab fees, OTC sales, plus licensing or franchise fees for the turnkey clinic-in-a-pharmacy kit sold to independents.
non_obvious_insight: Don't compete with telehealth on convenience; win on adjacency. Consult plus dispense in one stop removes the biggest leak in cash-pay care, which is people who get a prescription and never fill it. The fastest route isn't building stores at all. It is converting existing independents on the edge of closure by giving them a second revenue line, and an already-licensed pharmacy removes months of setup.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 independent pharmacies in Latino neighborhoods (Texas, Florida or Illinois). Contract per-diem NPs under a collaborative practice agreement, build a 100 sq ft consult room, and print a simple price list ('$29 visit, $4 generics'). Market through WhatsApp groups, churches and community radio. Run a 60-day pilot and track visit-to-fill conversion and margin per visit.

title: Remote Load Calcs That Avoid Panel Upgrades
one_liner: A photo-and-utility-bill service that proves an existing electrical panel can take a heat pump or EV charger, with load-management devices when it cannot.
customer: HVAC and heat-pump contractors, EV-charger installers and solar-plus-storage installers without in-house electricians. Later: state and utility electrification programs.
problem: Data centers are absorbing electricians (nearly a third of the shortage; Texas builders report electrical delays of up to 2 months). Residential electrician time becomes the scarcest input, so panel upgrades stall every electrification job. HVAC contractors selling heat pumps are blocked by work they do not do and cannot schedule. The HVAC rebound expected in 2027 will make it worse.
solution: Installer uploads a photo of the panel label plus 12 months of utility data. The service returns a permit-ready load calculation under the existing-load method, stamped by a remote licensed engineer or electrician. It recommends the cheapest path: no upgrade, a load-management or circuit-pausing device allowed by recent NEC editions, or a smart panel, with the material list for the installer's quote.
why_now: Electrician scarcity from data-center overtime ($130-170K, vendor stat), 2027 HVAC rebound with A2L certification adding friction, and a 110K technician shortage. Load-management devices and energy-management provisions are now commercially available and code-recognized in many places.
revenue_model: $79-149 per calculation billed to installers. Annual contracts with programs. Referral margin from load-management device makers.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for electrification is neither the heat pump nor the HVAC tech, it is the panel and the electrician-days it consumes. Avoiding electrician hours is worth more than adding them, and the existing truck-roll panel check can be done as a $99 desk job by one remote engineer serving many installers.
first_30_days: Sign 20 HVAC contractors in one state. Contract a licensed PE or master electrician for templates and stamps. Deliver 50 calculations by hand. Measure the percentage that avoided an upgrade.

title: Drone Incident Desk for Cities and Venues
one_liner: Detection-to-handoff service that turns a drone sighting into a documented, legally routed federal referral for local agencies that cannot legally jam anything.
customer: City emergency management and police departments, stadium and arena operators, and event promoters at major events. Dallas has $10M set aside, and FEMA has a $500M counter-UAS grant program.
problem: Insiders see counter-drone as a radar and jammer hardware sale. Local police mostly lack legal authority to mitigate, and protocols with FBI and DHS are unclear. FBI and DHS seized more than 700 drones near one stadium during the World Cup. Cities are buying sensors with no playbook for what to do next.
solution: Vendor-neutral software plus a 24/7 human desk. It ingests alerts from whatever sensors a venue owns (RF, Remote ID, radar) and classifies them. It geolocates the pilot, routes the incident to the correct federal or state authority, and packages a chain-of-custody evidence file. Includes tabletop drills and after-action reports.
why_now: The World Cup exposed the gap. FEMA counter-UAS grant money is arriving at localities. Future mega-events raise urgency, and Remote ID data is now broadly available.
revenue_model: Annual subscription per venue or city ($40-150K), event-surge packages, and drill or training fees. It also helps grant applicants justify sensor purchases.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is purchasing liability cover and a working relationship with federal agencies, not detection accuracy. Sensors will commoditize, but the handoff protocol and evidence trail will not.
first_30_days: Interview 10 emergency managers and venue security directors in World Cup host cities. Build the desk on a shared inbox plus a case-management tool. Offer a free tabletop exercise to 3 venues and convert one to a paid pilot.

title: Consented Elder-Speech Data Co-op via Storytelling Clubs
one_liner: Senior-living oral-history clubs where residents opt in, get a life-story book and pay, and their de-identified speech is licensed under strict speech-recognition-only, no-cloning terms to voice-AI and ambient-scribe companies.
customer: Speech-AI, ambient clinical documentation, hearing-aid and companion-robot teams buying elder-speech training and test data (per audio hour). Senior-living operators host the clubs for engagement and a revenue share, and families receive the recordings.
problem: Voice and scribe AI is tuned on younger speech and underperforms on 80+ voices, hearing-aid users and dementia, Parkinson's or stroke speech. AI labs now need clean chain-of-title (Suno swapped to a licensed-data model on Sep 9), and older adults are adopting AI (23% of 65+) while distrusting how their data is used (69% of 50+ are uncomfortable sharing health records with AI). The people who could supply ethical data, and who deserve to be paid for it, have no rights infrastructure.
solution: Trained facilitators (retired teachers, social workers) run recorded storytelling sessions in senior-living communities. Every participant passes a capacity screen with a family or health-care-proxy co-signature and can withdraw. Each clip carries a machine-readable consent scope (recognition and understanding only, never voice synthesis or cloning), is de-identified, and is tracked in a rights ledger that supports revocation and audit. Residents receive cash, the community gets a share, and families get an edited memoir and audio archive.
why_now: Licensed-data pressure is peaking after music and text lawsuits, and the EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency rules began applying in Aug 2026. Voice AI is being pushed on seniors just as they adopt it, and the 80+ cohort is the fastest growing group in the country.
revenue_model: Buyers pay roughly $80-150 per audio hour under a per-dataset license. About 25-30% goes to participants, 15% to the host community, and the rest covers facilitators and platform costs. Family memoir and archive packages are a $149-299 upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not more hours of speech. It is consented hours from the oldest speakers, and only eldercare operators can gather them ethically, because capacity screening, proxies and revocation are the whole product. The strictest license terms (recognition only, no cloning) are what let elders and families say yes.
first_30_days: Pilot in 3 communities with an ethics review from a local university IRB or elder-law adviser. Record about 40 hours and secure a letter of intent from 2 to 3 elder-focused voice or scribe teams for a 100-hour dataset. Use the memoir book as the participant-facing hook.

title: Executor-of-Last-Resort for Solo Agers
one_liner: A subscription that names a licensed fiduciary as your executor and runs daily wellness checks, so a childless retiree isn't found weeks late and handed to a court-appointed stranger.
customer: Unpartnered or childless adults 65+ with $100K-$1.5M estates (too small for most corporate trustees, too large to ignore), plus their elder-law attorneys, senior living communities and Area Agencies on Aging.
problem: Solo agers have no obvious executor, agent or emergency contact, and named friends or nieces often flake. Japan shows the downstream effect: 37,227 people living alone were found dead at home in H1 2024, nearly 4,000 undiscovered for over a month. The US has no equivalent service layer, and intestate estates go to public administrators.
solution: A 'Stewardship Plan'. (a) A licensed professional fiduciary or trust company partner agrees to serve as successor agent and executor. (b) Passive wellness signals (phone, smart speaker, utility use, optional wearable) plus a daily automated or human check-in escalate to neighbors and welfare checks. (c) A digital go-bag holds accounts, medications, pets, keys and funeral wishes. (d) At death it triggers funeral instructions, securing the house, clear-out and estate administration for a fee schedule.
why_now: Cheap ambient signals and voice-AI check-in calls make monitoring inexpensive. Death care is proving roll-up-able (Everstory, SCI), yet no one serves the years before death for people without heirs. Estates and consolidator data show volume is flat, so services attached to existing customers are where growth sits.
revenue_model: $39-$79/month subscription, executor fees at death (often statutory, a few percent of the estate), margin on clear-out and estate services, and B2B fees from senior living and AAAs.
non_obvious_insight: The first customer isn't dying. She is buying certainty that someone competent shows up on the worst day. Subscriptions fund the acquisition of a low-cost executor book that pays out later.
first_30_days: Partner with a licensed fiduciary in one state. Sign 3 elder-law attorneys. Recruit a 30-person waitlist through senior centers and 'elder orphan' groups. Charge $99 setup plus $49/month and run the daily check-in calls manually at first.

title: Lifetime Income Leases for Retiring Farmers' Water
one_liner: A 'water pension' that turns a retiring farm couple's senior Colorado River water right into guaranteed, inheritable lifetime income via a long-term forbearance lease, satellite-verified and sold as verified acre-feet to cities and corporates.
customer: Buyers are municipal water agencies, Lower Basin cities, corporate water-stewardship funds (such as the Water Resilience Coalition Amazon put $20M into) and conservation programs. Sellers are farm owners 62+ without farming heirs. Money moves as multi-year lease payments, and the firm keeps 8-12%.
problem: About 70% of the Colorado River goes to agriculture, and the 2027-2036 framework (Record of Decision, Aug 2026) forces the next cuts onto farms, with Powell and Mead near 36% full. 'Buy-and-dry' sales are politically toxic. Lump-sum sales trigger capital gains and do not fund a long retirement, and urban heirs inherit water rights they cannot operate. Buyers want verified acre-feet, but no settlement layer exists.
solution: A 15-30-year forbearance (rotational fallowing or deficit irrigation) on a slice of the right. Payments are indexed and pass to the surviving spouse, then to a trust. An estate-plan wrapper (trust holds the right with the lease attached, plus CPA and water-attorney advice on tax basis and long-term-care planning) makes it a retirement product. Consumptive-use reduction is verified by satellite evapotranspiration data and paid quarterly. Title never leaves the family, which defuses buy-and-dry politics for the buyer.
why_now: The 10-year framework was finalized in Aug 2026 and storage is the lowest since 1963. Corporate money is arriving ($32M raised toward a $100M goal) with no settlement layer. US drought coverage is 49.6%. A generation of irrigators is reaching retirement with no successors.
revenue_model: 8-12% of lease flows, a buyer-paid verification subscription per acre-foot, and a $3-5k planning fee per family.
non_obvious_insight: Older water-right owners often refuse to sell at any price but will accept certainty of income for life while keeping title. Water brokers are paid on transfers, not on retirements, so nobody sells water as a pension asset. The retirement-income framing is what makes the supply available.
first_30_days: Pick one district (Palo Verde Valley CA, Yuma AZ or Grand Valley CO). Run three kitchen-table workshops with an ag lender, a CPA and a water attorney to enroll about 10 couples. Get a non-binding letter of intent from one buyer for 500-2,000 acre-feet. Check the state rules on temporary transfers first.
